insights.headline: RBI hike in sight as gold steadies above $4,150; GST rejig weighed on bullion importers
insights.summary: The RBI's October 7 decision is the domestic focal point, with markets pricing a 25 bps hike as inflation risks mount and the rupee closing at 96.42. Globally, gold climbed above $4,150 as Treasury yields eased and October Fed hike bets faded, while the annual LBMA survey sees gold at $5,013 and silver at $97 within a year. The GST Council is weighing a 3% GST on gold that could strip MMTC and STC of their import tax edge, central banks added 39 tonnes of gold in August, and ICE launched gold futures trading in London.
points: RBI's October 7 call is the domestic focal point, with a 25 bps hike priced in as inflation risks rise and the rupee at 96.42.
Gold rose above $4,150 as Treasury yields eased and October Fed hike odds faded; traders await Wednesday's FOMC minutes.
LBMA delegates expect gold at $5,013 and silver at $97 over the next 12 months, per the annual survey.
A proposed 3% gold GST could remove the import tax advantage of MMTC and STC.
Central banks bought 39 tonnes of gold in August; ICE began gold futures trading in London.

trending.title: RBI's first hike in almost four years
trending.summary: Markets have priced a 25 bps increase at the October 7 meeting as inflation risks mount, pressuring the rupee to 96.42 and keeping domestic bullion sentiment cautious.

trending.title: London finally gets a gold futures market
trending.summary: ICE began trading physically-linked gold, silver, platinum and palladium futures in the $190bn-a-day physical hub, a fresh attempt after the LME's 2022 exit.

trending.title: Producers join the hoarding
trending.summary: From Laos refining to Indonesia's planned 15% export tax, gold-producing countries are keeping more metal at home, echoing central banks' de-dollarization buying.

trending.title: Diwali demand meets cautious buyers
trending.summary: Festive buying is underway but high prices are keeping shoppers watchful, with Dubai prices slipping ahead of Navratri and Diwali while Titan's jewellery sales grew 21%.

trending.title: Silver's supply pipeline builds
trending.summary: Discovery cleared federal environmental permits for Mexico's giant Cordero silver project, even as brokerages debate a 2027 surplus and silver holds a base above $60.

items.title: RBI MPC interest rate decision in focus: Can a 25 bps hike trigger a market sell-off?
items.summary: The RBI's monetary policy decision on October 7 is the market's focal point, with traders pricing in a 25-basis-point rate hike as inflation risks mount. Analysts are assessing whether the first hike in nearly four years could spark a sell-off in equities and what it means for the rupee and bond yields.

items.title: MMTC, STC may lose gold import tax advantage as GST Council weighs 3% GST
items.summary: The GST Council is likely to discuss on October 8 bringing government trading entities like MMTC and STC under the 3% GST net for precious-metal imports, ending a tax advantage held since 2017 and putting banks, nominated agencies and bullion exchanges on the same footing, the Times of India reports.

items.title: Gold to hit $5,000, silver $97 in the next 12 months - LBMA delegate survey
items.summary: Delegates at the 2026 LBMA Global Precious Metals Conference expect gold near $5,013 an ounce a year from now, about 20% above current spot, and silver near $94.70, Kitco reports; a UBS survey found 65% of reserve managers cite diversification as the main reason for holding gold.

items.title: Rupee loses 13 paise to close at 96.42 per US dollar
items.summary: The rupee closed 13 paise lower at 96.42 against the US dollar as foreign fund outflows weighed on the currency. Traders are watching the RBI's policy decision, with markets pricing in a 25-basis-point rate hike amid mounting inflation risks.

items.title: Gold Futures Regain Some Ground As U.S. Dollar, Yields Slip
items.summary: Front-month Comex gold settled up 0.75% at $4,159.20 an ounce and silver up 0.49% at $61.168, snapping a two-session losing streak as the dollar pulled back from an 18-month high and Treasury yields eased; Forex.com's Fawad Razaqzada cautioned the outlook stays fragile with yields elevated and oil-rebound risk.

items.title: Gold, Silver Edge Higher On MCX As Fed Rate-Hike Bets Ease
items.summary: Bullion edged higher on MCX after softer US jobs data eased October Fed rate-hike bets; December gold futures traded around ₹1,49,212 per 10 grams and December silver near ₹2,26,322 per kg by mid-afternoon, though elevated Treasury yields capped gains ahead of the Oct 27-28 FOMC meeting.

items.title: NYSE Owner Launches Gold Futures in London
items.summary: Intercontinental Exchange has begun trading gold, silver, platinum and palladium futures in London, the world's leading physical bullion hub, with contracts linked to the daily auctions it operates. It is the latest attempt to build a viable gold futures market in London after the LME shut its contract in 2022.

items.title: Central banks add 39 net tonnes of gold in August with China, Uzbekistan and Poland leading purchases
items.summary: Central banks bought a net 39 tonnes of gold in August, taking reported 2026 purchases to 170 tonnes, World Gold Council data via Kitco shows; China added 20 tonnes in its 22nd straight month of buying while Uzbekistan and Poland bought 8 tonnes each, with Poland nearing its 700-tonne reserve target.

items.title: The World's Gold Producers Are Starting to Hoard Their Own Gold
items.summary: Asian gold-producing countries are keeping more metal at home through domestic refining, export taxes and central bank buying of local output, per a Nikkei Asia report. Indonesia plans up to a 15% gold export tax from 2026, while China's central bank extended its buying streak — a resource-nationalism trend that could tighten global supply.

items.title: Gold, silver edge higher on MCX: Key levels to watch
items.summary: Gold and silver traded higher on MCX on Tuesday, extending the recovery from September's correction as soft US payrolls eased October Fed-hike bets; analysts flagged key support and resistance levels to watch ahead of the Oct 27-28 FOMC meeting.

items.title: Discovery Announces Receipt of Key Environmental and Land Use Permits for Cordero Project
items.summary: Discovery Mining has received the environmental impact and land-use permits from Mexico's SEMARNAT for its Cordero project, completing the federal environmental approval process. Cordero, in Chihuahua state, is described as one of the world's largest undeveloped silver deposits, and the company can now advance it toward development.

items.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD builds base above $60, eyes $64
items.summary: Silver is building a base above $60, up over 1% to $61.13 after bouncing off $60.36 lows, FXStreet's technical desk notes; a break above $62 opens the way toward $64–65 resistance, while a drop below the Oct 2 low of $59.69 would turn the short-term bias bearish.

items.title: Gold-silver ratio at 68: Gold looks expensive, but should investors stay invested?
items.summary: The gold-silver ratio has risen to about 68:1, leaving gold looking expensive relative to silver, Moneycontrol reports; analysts quoted in the piece suggest long-term investors keep gold as the core holding and consider adding silver if the ratio starts declining with improving silver demand.

items.title: Silver may enter surplus by 2027 from supply deficit; brokerages see prices consolidating
items.summary: Brokerages expect silver's long-running supply deficit to narrow through 2026 and the market to flip into surplus by 2027, which should keep prices consolidating rather than extending the rally; 12-month brokerage targets on MCX sit around ₹3.5–4 lakh per kg, CNBC-TV18 reports.

items.title: Gold corrects 26% from January record high — is this a buying opportunity ahead of Diwali?
items.summary: Gold is down more than 26% from its January record of $5,595 an ounce to around $4,100, pressured by multi-decade-high US Treasury yields and a firm dollar; analysts at Kotak Securities, Choice Broking and Tata Mutual Fund say valuations have turned more attractive and the festive/Diwali season could offer an entry window.

items.title: Gold price dips, but buyers remain cautious ahead of Diwali
items.summary: Gold in Pune has fallen nearly Rs 8,000 per 10 grams over the past month to about Rs 1.47 lakh, yet buyers remain cautious ahead of Diwali, the Times of India reports; shoppers are shifting to lighter designs while Augmont's Renisha Chainani says many are still waiting on the sidelines.

items.title: Titan Q2FY27 update: Consumer businesses grow 25% YoY, jewellery up 21%
items.summary: Titan's consumer businesses grew 25% year-on-year in Q2FY27 excluding bullion, with jewellery up 21%, watches 30%, EyeCare 28% and international business 97%; the company added 78 net stores, a strong signal of jewellery demand heading into the festive season.

items.title: Dubai gold prices drop further ahead of Indian festivals Navratri, Diwali
items.summary: Dubai gold slipped further on Tuesday, with 24K at Dh496.75 a gram at the open — below Dh500 — prompting early festive buying by NRI families ahead of Navratri and Diwali; Pepperstone's Chris Weston says the short-term investment case for gold remains weak.
